title: Best Medicare Supplement Insurance 2026: 5 Plan G Carriers
description: Mutual of Omaha, Aetna, Humana, Blue Cross Blue Shield, UnitedHealthcare AARP — quoted for the same 65-year-old in Florida, Texas, and California. Plan G is the standard; here's how carriers stack up.
lede: Five Medicare Supplement carriers. Same 65-year-old non-smoker. We pulled real quotes for Plan G in Florida, Texas, and California — the three states where premium differences are widest. Tracked premium, rate-increase history, customer service, and bundled extras.
methodology: Same applicant: 65-year-old non-smoker, healthy. Quoted Plan G (most popular post-2020) in FL, TX, CA. Tracked annual premium, 5-year rate-increase history, Better Business Bureau rating, and bundled benefits (SilverSneakers, hearing aid discounts, etc.).

sections.heading: What Plan G covers
paragraphs: Plan G covers everything Original Medicare doesn't, EXCEPT the Part B deductible ($240/year in 2026). Plan F (which covered Part B deductible) was discontinued for new enrollees in 2020.
Plan G is the most popular for new enrollees post-2020 because it covers the same expensive gaps (Part A deductible, Part B coinsurance, etc.) at lower premium than Plan F historical cost.
Plan G alternatives: Plan N (lower premium, $20 copay per office visit + $50 ER copay) for healthy seniors who don't visit doctors often. Plan G is the safe default.

sections.heading: Premium by carrier and state
paragraphs: 65-year-old Plan G monthly premium by state and carrier: Florida averages $180-220 (highest), Texas $130-170, California $150-200. Florida's high premiums are due to retirement demographics and hurricane risk.
Cheapest carrier in our test: Aetna $140-190/mo across states. Most expensive: Blue Cross Blue Shield $160-220/mo (varies by state BCBS).

Rate-increase history (5 years): UnitedHealthcare AARP averaged 4-6% annual increases, Mutual of Omaha 5-7%, Aetna 5-8%, Humana 4-7%, BCBS varies widely by state. Rate stability matters more than initial premium for long-term holders.

sections.heading: Bundled benefits and customer service
paragraphs: Bundled extras: Aetna includes SilverSneakers gym membership (worth $25-50/mo equivalent), free hearing aid discounts, vision discounts. UnitedHealthcare AARP includes Renew Active (gym + brain games). Mutual of Omaha includes basic discount programs. Humana and BCBS more limited extras.
Customer service ratings (BBB + AM Best): UnitedHealthcare A+ AM Best, Mutual of Omaha A+ AM Best, Aetna A AM Best, Humana A AM Best, BCBS varies by state.
Pre-existing condition treatment: Medicare Supplement is guaranteed issue ONLY during Open Enrollment (first 6 months after Part B starts). Outside that window, carriers can underwrite — and decline.

faqs.a: Plan G if you want zero out-of-pocket beyond Part B deductible. Plan N (cheaper premium) if you accept $20 copay per doctor visit + $50 ER copay. Plan N saves ~20% premium for healthy seniors who don't visit doctors often.
During your 6-month Open Enrollment Period starting the month Part B becomes effective. Guaranteed issue (no underwriting). Outside this window, carriers can deny you for health conditions.
Yes, but outside Open Enrollment carriers can underwrite. Some states have annual 'Birthday Rules' or 'Anniversary Rules' that let you switch carriers without underwriting.

Medicare Supplement (Medigap): Use any Medicare doctor nationwide, higher premium ($150-200/mo), predictable costs. Medicare Advantage: Network restrictions, lower premium (often $0), variable out-of-pocket costs. Pick by whether you value flexibility or low monthly cost.

mutual-of-omaha-medicare-supplement.review: Mutual of Omaha Medicare Supplement is the right pick for stability-focused buyers. Mutual company (policyholders share dividends), A+ AM Best rating, Plan G $150-200/mo. Rate-increase history is moderate. Strong long-term carrier.
cons: Not always cheapest in your state

aetna-medicare-supplement.review: Aetna Medicare Supplement (CVS Health) is the right pick if you value bundled extras. SilverSneakers gym membership included, hearing aid discounts, vision discounts. Cheapest in our test ($140-190/mo across states). Owned by CVS Health.

humana-medicare-supplement.review: Humana Medicare Supplement is a solid mid-tier option. Plan G $145-200/mo, strong Medicare Advantage cross-sell if you ever want to switch. Available in most states. Less aggressive on bundled extras but reliable.

blue-cross-blue-shield-medicare-suppleme.review: Blue Cross Blue Shield Medicare Supplement is the right pick if you want the largest network in your state. State-specific BCBS plans vary in pricing — some states have very competitive BCBS pricing, others are highest in test. Check your state.
pros: Largest provider network in most states
cons: AM Best rating varies by state BCBS

united-healthcare-aarp-medicare-suppleme.review: UnitedHealthcare AARP Medicare Supplement is the largest single Medicare Supplement insurer in the US. AARP-endorsed, A+ AM Best rating, includes Renew Active (gym + brain games). Plan G $150-210/mo. Strong stability and brand recognition.
cons: Brand premium may not be worth the extra cost

offerNotes.mutual-of-omaha-medicare-supplement: Quote through Mutual of Omaha advisors. Long history of dividend-paying.
offerNotes.humana-medicare-supplement: Quote at humana.com — solid mid-tier option.
offerNotes.blue-cross-blue-shield-medicare-suppleme: Quote at bcbs.com — pricing varies dramatically by state BCBS.
offerNotes.united-healthcare-aarp-medicare-suppleme: Quote at aarpmedicaresupplement.com — AARP endorsement required (AARP membership $16/year).

pinDescription: Best Medicare Supplement 2026: Mutual of Omaha vs Aetna vs Humana vs BCBS vs UnitedHealthcare AARP — Plan G quoted across 3 states. #medicaresupplement

recommendedFor.label: Retirees who prioritize long-term premium stability
recommendedFor.reason: Mutual of Omaha's A+ AM Best rating and mutual company structure make it the safest long-term bet for buyers who plan to hold their policy for decades.

recommendedFor.label: Active seniors who exercise and use hearing or vision care
recommendedFor.reason: Aetna bundles SilverSneakers gym membership plus hearing aid and vision discounts — extras that offset its premium cost for health-conscious seniors.

recommendedFor.label: Snowbirds and seniors who travel between multiple states
recommendedFor.reason: BCBS holds the largest provider network in most states, so you'll find in-network doctors whether you're wintering in Florida or spending summers up north.

recommendedFor.label: Budget-conscious new Medicare enrollees on fixed income
recommendedFor.reason: Humana's mid-tier pricing ($145-200/mo) and wide state availability make it a reliable entry point without overpaying for bundled extras you may not use.

recommendedFor.label: AARP members who want the most recognized national brand
recommendedFor.reason: UnitedHealthcare's AARP endorsement, A+ AM Best rating, and Renew Active program appeal to seniors who want a household name with built-in wellness perks.
